In the Aeneid, Juno offers this deity the hand of the nymph Deiopea in exchange for his help. This figure ordered his daughter Canace to kill herself after she committed incest with his son Macareus. According to some sources, this deity is the son of a woman who was born as a foal, although others claim him to be a son of Hippotes. In some stories, this figure and his brother Boeotus were conceived when Poseidon impregnated Arne while in the form of a bull. This deity is perhaps best known for giving a bag to a wanderer and telling him not to open it; ignorance of that command resulted in Eurus, Notus, and Boreas flying out of the bag and wrecking the ships belonging to Odysseus. Name this inhabitant of a floating island and Greek ruler of the winds.

A shrine dedicated to this god was guarded by birds that shot darts from their feathers. This god tried to join the Trojan War to avenge the death of his son Ascalaphus at the hands of Deiphobus, but he was stopped by Athena. A son of this god was dragged to death by his horses after losing a chariot race to Pelops. This deity slew Halirrhothius as revenge for the rape of his daughter Alcippe, resulting in the first murder trial in history. This deity was wounded in the thigh by Heracles after attempting to avenge the death of Cycnus. This god was trapped in a bronze urn for thirteen months by the Aloadae until being freed by Hermes. Hephaestus used a net to catch Aphrodite in bed with this figure, who was often accompanied in battle by Deimos and Phobos. Name this Greek god of war.

This man became the leader of his group after killing the repeated arsonist of Tara, Aillen. This man invited Diarmuid to a boar hunt and refused to save him as he lay dying. This man may have been killed at the Battle of Gabhair while grieving his grandson Oscar, and his son supposedly fled the battle and relayed the story to the Bishop of Armagh. This figure's son was taken to Tír na nÓg, where he lived for three hundred years, immediately transforming into an old man upon his return. Three sounds of this man's hunting horn will supposedly wake this father of Oisín to defend his country. As a boy, this figure burned his fingers while helping his mentor Finnegas cook the Salmon of Knowledge. Name this legendary Irish warrior and leader of the Fianna.

One being in this myth system lost some of his power after the Elders plucked out his pupils, and one race of people in this mythology had their heads lopped off by vampire bats after they failed to recognize the power of their creator, the Heart of Heaven. One place in this mythology can only be accessed after crossing a river of scorpions, a river of blood, and a river of pus. A woman in this system was impregnated when a decapitated skull spat on her, and the resulting children used a crab to lure the prideful demon Zipacna to his death. Figures in this myth system include the Bacabs, the Camazotz and Seven-Macaw, and it contains an underworld called Xibalba. Name this mythology recounted in the Popol Vuh that describes stories of K'iche' people and includes tales of the Hero Twins.

A daughter of Achelous named Eurymedousa was seduced by Zeus in the form of this animal, and the gold-mining Indikoi were said to be this type of creature. A monster spawned in the Libyan desert from the Medusa's blood was known as the Mother of these animals. An Aesop's fable relates how Zeus once turned a greedy farmer into one of these animals. After Hera's jealousy of Aegina led her to send a plague on her namesake island, Aeacus prayed to Zeus to transform these animals into people. Daedalus was discovered by Minas after solving a riddle involving one of these animals and a seashell, and a king who later assisted the drunken satyr Silenus was fed by a procession of these creatures as a child. A multitude of these animals also helped Psyche sort a mix of grains into separate heaps. Name these insects which were transformed into the Myrmidons.

One of this figure's sons is depicted with a wounded wrist in a painting by Polygnotus in the Lesche at Delphi. This figure purified Amphitryon of his blood guilt after the murder of Electryon. This figure's son Megareus battled against Eteoclus at the gate of Neïs, where Megareus was killed. This father of Lycomedes and Megara once claimed that "the whole breed of prophets certainly loves money," denying Tiresias's suggestion that he was opposing the will of the gods. The suicide of his son Haemon led his wife Eurydice to kill herself. This figure clashed with Antigone when he ordered that the corpse of Polyneices be left to rot on the battlefield as punishment for treason. Name this king of Thebes who offered the hand of his sister Jocasta in marriage to anyone who could free the city from the Sphinx, leading Oedipus to fulfill a prophecy.

This figure learned how to sing and dance from Chitrasena, a skill that became useful when he spent a year as the eunuch Brihannala in the kingdom of Virata. This figure's son died because he knew how to enter the Chakravyuha battle formation, but did not know how to exit. He shot the eye of a moving fish while only looking at its reflection to win the hand of his wife. This figure avenged the death of Abhimanyu by killing Jayadratha, and he helped Agni burn down the Khandava forest, receiving a chariot bearing the flag of Hanuman and the Gandiva bow in return. This favorite student of Drona killed Karna and shared his wife Draupadi with his brothers on the orders of his mother Kunti. Name this Pandava and hero of the Mahabharata who receives advice from his charioteer Krishna in the Bhagavad Gita.

In the Kalevala, Kullervo transforms some cattle into wolves and these creatures, resulting in the death of Ilmarinen's wife. One of these creatures married Hwanung and gave birth to Dangun, the founder of the Gojoseon kingdom. Polyphonte fell in love with one of these creatures, resulting in the birth of Agrius and Oreius. The Arkteia festival at Brauron involved girls imitating these creatures to appease Artemis. Although it is not a monkey, one of these animals named Jambavan served as an advisor to Sugriva, an ally of Rama. Ilmarinen builds a spear for Väinämöinen so he may slay one of these creatures named Otso; that one is often referred to as "honey-paws." A daughter of Lycaon who was transformed into one of these animals was the mother of Arcas by Zeus. Name these animals exemplified by Callisto, who was placed among the stars as Ursa Major.

This man avoided a fight against a giant by disguising himself as a baby, causing the giant to flee in fear of the man who could father such a large baby. This man stuck a poisoned spear into his head to keep himself awake in the face of some sleep-inducing harp music from a demon who came once a year to burn down the palace of Tara. This man hunted with two humans transformed into hounds named Bran and Sceolan, who helped this man acquire a wife who had been turned into a deer. That wife, Sadhbh, gave birth to this hero's son Oisin. Name this white haired Irish hero who could suck on his thumb to gain knowledge after he burned it on the Salmon of Wisdom.

This figure once had a nightmare where she used the blood of a murdered man to put out an inferno in her house. Nonnus calls her the mother of Faunus by Poseidon. Picus's rejection of this woman resulted in him being changed into a woodpecker, and following Glaucus's rejection of her, she sprinkled special herbs in bathwater to turn Scylla into a monster. This inhabitant of Aiaia purified her niece of murder and was thwarted with the moly plant, which Hermes gave to Odysseus. Identify Medea's sorceress aunt who changed Odysseus's men into swine.

Little-Bear's Son switches this figure's Strong Water for Weak Water and defeats her. She ages a year every time someone asks her a question and restores her youth by drinking a tea made from blue roses. She beats up three giants named Mustache-man, Hill-man, and Oak-man, but is thwarted by two orphans who use a comb that turns into a forest. She owns a herd of mares that fly like birds, one of which was stolen during a quest to rescue the woman warrior Maria from a wizard known as the Deathless. People who escape being eaten by her include Prince Ivan and Vasilissa the Beautiful. Often seen flying in a mortar and pestle or chillaxing in a house on chicken legs, name this witch from Russian folklore.

This deity lived apart from his wife after he was not comfortable with her home Thrymheim. In the Lokasenna, Loki claims that the daughters of Hymir used this deity as a pisspot. This god supposedly had an incestuous relationship with his sister, who may correspond to the Germanic goddess Nerthus. This god owns the hall Noatun, and he is married to the goddess who placed a snake dripping venom above Loki's head. That wife of this god is the daughter of Thiazi, and she mistakenly selected this god for marriage, thinking that he was Baldr because of his beautiful feet. Skadi married what Vanir god of seafaring, the father of Frey and Freya?

Thessandrus and Sthenelus were given command of this object, which was the subject of an argument between Thymoetes and Capys. This object was circled three times by a queen who imitated other women's voices, and its creation was overseen by Epeius on Mount Ida. It was put into use after the theft of the Palladium removed divine protection from its target. A priest who hurled a spear at the side of this object was strangled by serpents along with his sons; that priest was Laocoon. Identify this large, hollow, wooden sculpture designed by Odysseus to infiltrate a namesake city.

Zeus piled Mount Sipylus on top of Pandareus for stealing a dog from this locale and giving it to Tantalus, and Procris received a dog from this place that was later turned to stone by Zeus. Homer said that there were one hundred cities here, and according to Hesiod, Adrastia and Ida nursed a young Zeus in this place. After the Trojan War, Idomeneus returned home to this place, which was defended by a figure who died when Poeas shot him in the ankle or when Medea removed a pin, allowing ichor to flow out of the defender's bronze body. In addition to Talos, this island was home to a monster who ate fourteen Athenian children each year. Identify this island on which Theseus descended into the Labyrinth to kill the Minotaur.

In one story, this figure steals fruit from a tree by disrupting the balance of metal within it. At one point, he is banished by his master because he appears to have killed a young girl, her mother, and her father, who were actually disguises of a shape-shifting bone demon. His eyes are particularly susceptible to smoke, and he can be subdued with a chant that causes his headband to tighten. He was sealed under a mountain for five centuries as punishment for causing havoc in heaven, and can jump 108,000 li in a single somersault. Name this disciple of the priest San Zang who leads a group of primates on the Island of Flowers and Fruit, a main character in Journey to the West.

According to some sources, this figure has a head made of flint, and he lies in wait on Mt. Bakhu. This figure was often depicted fighting a cat who protects the ished tree, and he is shown with his head to the ground at gate two of the underworld and chained by his neck at gate ten in the Book of Gates. He was born from the primeval waters of Nun and the saliva of Neith. The only god who can resist this entity's hypnotic gaze is Set, who defends the Solar Barque against him. Name this snake god of chaos who fights Ra every night.

This figure fathered the nymph Canens with Venilia. An altar to this god was one of two featured in the rite of the Tigillum Sororium. Carna once tried to hide from him in a bush but this god raped her and transformed her into the goddess Cardea. This god shared his kingdom with Saturn when Saturn fled from Greece, and he caused a hot spring to erupt to fend off an attack by the Sabine men against Rome. In times of peace his temple's doors were closed, but in times of war they were perpetually open. Name this two-faced god to whom the beginning of the year is dedicated.

This figure was said to have been born when an eagle shot an arrow into an insect, and he travels from village to village chasing away the winter and snow, bringing spring and rain. Depictions of this god include a traveling salesman, insect, musician, warrior and a hunting magician. His union with Ice Flower produced the spiritual leader of the Eagle Clan. He carries a sack of clouds full of rainbows or seeds in Navajo legends, and he floats down rivers, impregnating bathing women with his detachable phallus. Name this hunchbacked trickster god of the American Southwest.

Some of these creatures left their ancestral home and wandered about looking for a new home on the sands; that group of these creatures included the predecessors of Lofarr. One of these creatures died on the largest ship in the world. The first of these creatures was Motsognir, who was created from the blood of Brimir and the bones of Blainn. In the Gylfaginning, four of them support the four cardinal directions. Freyja slept with four of them known as the Brisings; their other members include the Sons of Ivaldi, who created Skibladnir and Gungir. Name this race of talented blacksmiths from Norse mythology who created Mjolnir.

An object guarded by one of these figures is also protected by Serket. These figures were among the seven guardians of Osiris's body, and they also formed the bowl of the Big Dipper. These gods were described as pillars of Shu, and were each associated with one of the cardinal directions. One of these deities, Duamutef, claims that he comes to rescue Osiris from an assailant, and another, Imsety, has the role of lifting up corpses. Name quartet of gods who guarded the Canopic Jars, who were said to be children of the son of Osiris and Isis.

Some sources say that this god's maternal grandfather is the giant Geirrendour. It is said that this god suckled on the milk of a male boar and the saltwater of the waves after he was born at the edge of the Nine Worlds. He helped retrieve the Brisingamen by taking the form of a seal and fighting Loki. He is said to have the whitest skin of all the Aesir, and his nickname Gullintanni refers to his golden teeth. He rides the horse Gulltopr and wields the sword Hofund, and he carries the horn Gjallerhorn, with which he will summon the Aesir to Ragnarok. Name this Norse god, the guardian of Bifrost.

This figure created the Moon after his ten sons saved him from being eaten by a fish. In one story, this figure tricked a hog and a goat into saying the word "nine" on a hill that kills you if you say the word "nine", but was himself similarly tricked by Monkey. He started hiding in the corners of houses after he was brought low with the help of a cloak of vines decorated with flies made by Chameleon. He once caught a python, a leopard, some hornets, and a dwarf in order to obtain all the stories of the world from Nyame. Name this Ashanti trickster god, known as 'the Spider'.

Though neither Janus nor Cardea, this figure inaugurated the Athenian New Year, being capable of looking into the past and future at the same time. This figure was once owned by Atlas, but died on Mount Abas while serving a different master. According to Hesiod, this creature slept with his own mother and fathered the Hydra and the Sphinx by her. This child of Typhon and Echidna is represented by Sirius, and the herdsman Eurytion died trying to help this beast, who was clubbed to death by Heracles. Identify this lesser brother of Cerberus, a two-headed dog who guarded the cattle of Geryon.

This figure accused one lover of having been raised by tigers in the Caucuses, and that lover was compared to an oak tree in how resilient they were to this figure's pleas. The nurse Barce fetched this figure's sister to build a structure intended for a Moorish rite. This figure wove the garment in which Pallas was buried, and she rejected the love of a son of Hammon named Iarbas. Earlier, she became a widow when her brother Pygmalion murdered her husband Sychaeus. She cut an oxhide into thin strips to enclose a large plot of land, on which she founded a city. This sister of Anna committed suicide with a Trojan sword, and while on her funeral pyre she predicted the coming of Hannibal. Identify this queen of Carthage and lover of Aeneas.

This figure lived past the seventh mountain range at the end of the world, the domain of Utu. His eventual slayer offered him Ma-Tur, along with shoes, pebbles, and other things, in exchange for this figure's seven protective auras. This figure met his death after he was bound by thirteen winds sent by the god Shamash. While he was occupied, fifty unmarried men chopped down the Cedar Forest, which had been placed under the protection of this intestine- faced giant by Enlil. Name this demonic giant who was killed by Enkidu and Gilgamesh.

An execution technique named for these creatures that involves the cutting and breaking of the ribs is believed to be a method of sacrifice to Odin. The giant Hraesvelgr took the form of one of these creatures, as did another giant who ate a large portion of an ox, thereby angering Loki. That giant who occasionally took the shape of this animal caused the gods to age by kidnapping Idunn, and was named Thiassi. The hawk Vedrfolnir sits on one of these animals above Yggdrasil, and Heracles killed a vulture or one of these animals for eating Prometheus's liver. Identify this bird of prey, parts of which are found in a griffin.

In a former life this figure and his brother were gatekeepers of Vishnu who were expelled from Vishnu's home for refusing entry to the Sanatha Kumara. He purified himself by Lake Rakshastaal, after which he was granted protection from all but mortal men. Vishwakarma designed this figure's city, whose rule he usurped from his half-brother Kubera. Shiva gave him the sword Chandrahas, which he used to kill the vulture-god Jatayu while he was returning to his city of Lanka along with his kidnapped captive Sita. Name this Rakshasa, the primary antagonist of the Ramayana.

This figure slipped while skating and entered a trance in which he saw his foster-father's imprisonment. He won a race while riding an old nag by striking the rest of the horses with holly twigs and enchanting them to dance. He also outwitted the accomplished seducer Prince Rhun, helping convince King Maelgwn to release his foster-father Elphin. He received knowledge and poetic talent when he drank three drops from the cauldron of the witch Ceridwen. Gwion Bach was the birth name of what legendary Welsh bard?

This figure's epithets include Clymenus and Eubuleus. One of his lovers was transformed into a white poplar whose leaves were used to crown Heracles, who shot this figure with an arrow during the siege of Pylos. Another of his lovers was transformed into mint after being trampled by this god's wife. Homer called him anae eneron, and those who made offerings of sheep to him had to turn away their faces when doing so. Like Geryon, this god kept his cattle on Erytheia; unlike Geryon, he was married to a daughter of Demeter. He lent Perseus his magic helmet, which made the wearer invisible. Name this Greek god, the lord of the underworld.

In Cumbrian legends, this figure is a giant who founded Mallerstang Castle and tried to divert the Eden River to make a moat. He fell in love with Argan's wife, but was defeated in battle and forced to build a castle. He and his brother were exiled to Brittany and later returned to Britain to depose Constans' killer. He took his epithet from an omen of glory that appeared as a comet. He abandoned his siege of Terrabil in order to consummate his love for Gorlois' wife, going with Sir Ulfius and Merlin to find her at Tintagel. Name this king who disguised himself in order to sleep with Ygraine and father Arthur Pendragon.

Epimenides of Crete called this figure the child of Peiras and Styx. She was the mother of Scythes [skih-theez], who used his father Heracles' bow. She lived with the Arimi, though she gave birth to one child under a plane tree at the spring of Amymone. This Phorcid never aged, and she fed on raw human flesh in her cave until she was killed by Argus Panoptes. Her body was half beautiful nymph, half speckled serpent. She was the mother of a beast which lived in the Lernean lake and of a beast whose skin protected Heracles. Name this creature who gave birth to the Nemean Lion and many other monsters with her husband Typhon.

This figure was tricked by his opponent's servant into thinking his opponent would attack from below, so he placed his shield under his feet. After the fight, the sorceress Groa forgot to remove a piece of this figure's whetstone weapon from his opponent's forehead. He created an enormous fighting companion made of clay called Mist Calf, or Mokkurkalfi, who was dispatched by Thjalfi. His corpse pinned his opponent until Jarnsaxa's son Magni lifted his legs. Name this jotunn killed by Thor after he lost a race on his horse Gullfaxi.

Zethus and Amphion killed Dirce by tying her hair to one of these animals. According to some sources, Dionysus scared Hippolytus's horses by making one of these animals rise from the sea. Prometheus's salve of invincibility protected Jason from some bronze, fire-breathing ones. Another one ravaged the Marathonian plain until it was killed by Theseus. Poseidon gave a white one of these animals to Minos, whose refusal to sacrifice that animal resulted in Pasiphae falling in love with it. Name these male animals, one of which composed the upper half of the Minotaur.

This son of the giant Fornjot was sometimes identified with Freyr's father-in-law, the giant Gymir. This god is said to inhabit the island of Hlsey, where his servants include Eldir and Fimafeng. Thor and Tyr helped this god host a great feast by stealing a giant cauldron from the giant Hymir, and Loki captured the dwarf Andvari with the help of this god's wife, who loaned Loki her net. Name this father of nine billow maidens, the husband of Ran, who is, like Njord, a Norse god of the sea.

Hyries created a pool of tears after her son became one of these creatures. While Er was in the underworld, he saw Orpheus choose to become this animal. A man who buried his wife Proclia alive was turned into one of these animals by Poseidon after Achilles strangled him.When Nemesis fled Zeus at Rhamnus, he assumed this form and raped her, causing her to lay an egg. Tyndareus laid with his wife on the same day that Zeus seduced her in this form, fathering Polydeuces and Helen. Identify this bird, in whose form Zeus raped Leda.

These animals were said to be a primary food source for the twin-headed serpent known as the Amphisbaena. In the Brahmavaivatra Purana, a bunch of these animals turn out to be former incarnations of Indra. When Midas was young, his future wealth was signaled by these creatures putting grains of wheat in his mouth, and in another grain-related incident, these animals helped Psyche sort various grains for Venus. After a great plague, Zeus repopulated the country of Aegina with people spawned from these animals; their descendants fought under Achilles at Troy. Name these insects that became the Myrmidons.

Odysseus used one of these items to trick Protesilaus into thinking that he would not be the first Greek to step foot on the shores of Troy. Another of these items had depictions of a city at war and a city hosting marriages among several other images surrounded by the Ocean stream, as described in book 18 of the Iliad. One of these items covered in bronze and made with seven cow- hides was used against the Trojans in conjunction with a bow wielded by Teucer; that one was owned by Ajax the Greater. Another of these objects had as its centerpiece the severed head of Medusa, and was owned by Athena or Zeus. The Aegis was an example of what protective piece of equipment?

This deity's cult was moved to Itjtawy when Amenemhat I moved the capital there. She was commonly known as the "lady of life" and was often said to be the mother of Maahes. One of her cult centers was in the city of Teramu, known to the Greeks as Leontopolis. In one story, a cow-goddess takes this goddess's form in an attempt to destroy civilization, but was pacified after drinking beer colored to look like blood. Name this fierce Egyptian warrior goddess who was commonly depicted as a lion.

The wife of Psherenptah III prayed successfully to this god for a son after giving birth to three daughters. This deity replaced Nefertum in the Memphis Triad, and he was said to have been instrumental in bringing an end to a seven year long famine. He was syncretized with the Greek god Asclepius, and was a physician elevated to the position of the god of medicine and healing in the Egyptian pantheon. Name this royal architect under Djoser who was legendarily responsible for the construction of the Step Pyramids of Saqqara.

One of these figures dedicated the Ceryneian Hind to Artemis, who briefly turned her into a doe in a failed attempt to spare her from Zeus. The eldest of these figures lived in a cave on Mount Cyllene, and became the grandmother of Autolycus, who followed in her son's footsteps by becoming a notorious cattle-thief. Another one of these figures denied her husband proper funeral rites at his request. Their timely catasterism ended Orion's amorous pursuit of these sisters of the Hesperides. This group includes Taygeta, Hermes's mother Maia, and Merope, whose shame over her marriage to the mortal Sisyphus causes her to shine less brightly than the others. Name these seven sisters who are the namesake of a star cluster.

In one myth, this deity kicks the tail off a deer created from a piece of fat on a hilltop. Methods for propitiating this deity include pouring water into the mouth of a hunted carcass and diving into the sea to replicate the action of brushing hair. This goddess orders dogs to maul her treacherous father, prompting her father to invoke a curse that causes the earth to swallow them both. Her father Anguta beat her hands till her fingers fell off, becoming seals and whales. The underworld of Adlivun is ruled by what Inuit sea goddess?

This figure gave a speech concerning oars being replaced by reins and dolphins by horses at Thera. Arete aided this figure by revealing Alcinous's decision to relinquish this woman if she was found not to be a virgin. Acastus drove her out of Iolcus after she tricked Alcestis's sisters into cutting up their father Pelias. Her children's grave stood next to a wall at which another woman threw herself after this woman gave her a poisoned robe. This woman departed in a chariot pulled by dragons after killing Glauce and her own children, according to Euripides. Name this sorceress from Colchis who poisoned the dragon guarding the Golden Fleece and married Jason.

According to Livy, a shower of stones portended great fortune for Rome in the Second Punic War if King Attalus of Pergamum could be persuaded to send this deity's statue. In the Aeneid, this deity appears on a chariot drawn by lions to avert Turnus' assault on Aeneas' ships. The Roman Hilaria were festivals in honor of this deity, whose followers, the Corybantes, made lots of noise by playing cymbals and drums. She loved a son of Nana, but when he fell in love with another she drove him mad, and he castrated himself and perished. Attis was the consort of what originally Phrygian mother goddess?

This god was born when a pike fish containing the creator god was consumed by his mother. This deity and his father-in-law transformed into eagles in order to rescue his future wife, who was abducted by a three headed serpent in a chariot driven by creatures that were half horse, half crow. In one story, this figure was imprisoned in a dungeon for three hundred years, during which time a serpent abducted his three sisters. That serpent, which was considered the ruler of the underworld and the waters, was named Veles. Often depicted with weapons made from thunderstone, this is, what Slavic thunder god, the son of Percunatele?

One figure of this name was thrown out of a tower by his grandfather Sekkoros, but had his fall broken by an eagle. This hero kills a few stone giants, but is forced to cut down 300 trees afterward in order to cross the Waters of Death. This hero walks on the Road of the Sun through Mount Mashu before meeting Siduri, who directs him to a ferryman named Urshanabi. The temple prostitute Shamhat seduces his best friend, the wild man Enkidu. Name this "two-thirds god, one third man," a king of Uruk with a namesake Epic.

In a ceremony dedicated to this deity, a handsome war prisoner was chosen to live in luxury with four women for a year, after which he was sacrificed to this deity. The Great Bear constellation is said to be the footprints of this god, who presided over district schools known as the telpochcalli. The earth was created after this god successfully lured out a primordial monster that was part fish, part crocodile, and perpetually hungry; that monster was known as Cipactli, and the lure used by this god was his own foot, which he replaced with a piece of obsidian. Name this Aztec god known as the Lord of the Smoking Mirror, who drove away his rival Quetzalcoatl.

The hero Phorbas killed a bunch of these creatures on the island of Rhodes, and the Seven Against Thebes killed one of these creatures after it killed the child Opheltes. Metanira gave her son Triptolemus a chariot drawn by these creatures. Hermes stole the sinews of Typhon from one of these creatures named Delphyne, and the heads of one hundred of these sprang from Typhon's arms. In a dream, Clytemnestra gave birth to one that fed on her breast milk and clotted blood. The Sparti were born when Cadmus sowed the teeth of one which was sacred to Ares. Hera sent two of these creatures to attack the infant Heracles, who strangled them. For 10 point, identify these animals which comprised the tail of the Chimaera and the hair of the Gorgons, including Medusa.

This figure took the form of a red-haired boy in order to steal a magic cow from Mac Samthainn. Different myths claim that this figure's deadliest weapon was stabbed by a spear made by Goibniu, or hit by a sling-stone and turned against this deity's own army. He attempted to avoid his fate by using a crystal tower as a prison for his daughter Ethniu, but she was impregnated by Cian. During the second battle of Magh Tuireadh, he managed to kill Nuada before dying at the hands of his grandson Lugh. Name this king of the Fomorians, who had a destructive "Evil Eye" in the middle of his forehead.

Like Wadjet, this deity was viewed as the protector of Lower Egypt. Like Hathor, this deity was sometimes depicted holding an aegis in one hand and a sistrum in the other. Although not Sekhmet or Nut, this deity was sometimes considered to be the mother of the juvenile sun god, Nefertem. In Greece, this goddess was often identified with Artemis and was known as Alluros. The arrival of this goddess' sacred animal was considered good luck because it killed disease-carrying rodents. For 10 points name this cat-headed Egyptian deity.

According to one story, these figures resulted from a two-year-long pregnancy culminating in their mother giving birth to a hard lump of flesh, which was cut into pieces that were placed in jars of butter, out of which they emerged two years later. Following an unfair dice game, the second eldest member of this group tried to humiliate a woman by unwrapping her dress, but it kept getting longer, and the eldest member of this group humiliated that woman by making her sit on his thigh; their actions were later avenged by Bhima, who killed all the males of this group at Kurukshetra. Duryodhana was the eldest member of what group of 100 brothers who were descendants of Kuru that fought against the Pandavas?

When this goddess was parched, a group of people from whom she sought water denied her and soiled their water with mud; they were then condemned to live in their muddy pond. This daughter of Phoebe and Coeus took the form of a she-wolf to avoid the wrath of Hera while she was traveling from the Hyperboreans to a floating island, which was anchored by pillars after she gave birth there. This goddess's two children with Zeus were born on Ortygia and Delos, and they shot arrows at the seven sons and seven daughters of Niobe. Identify this goddess, who was assisted by her daughter Artemis in giving birth to her son Apollo.

This figure provided an underground palace built by Hephaestus to Oenopion, which prevented Orion from finding Oenopion. He fathered ten sons with Cleito, whom he enclosed with three giant ditches so that no mortal could reach her, and he fathered Despoena and Arion after joining the herd of Oncus and raping his sister. This god's son by Thoosa sang a song to Galatea, and after this god raped Caenis, he turned her into the powerful male warrior Caeneus. This god fathered Chrysaor on Medusa, as well as Chrysaor's brother Pegasus; he also fathered Triton by his wife Amphitrite. Identify this father of Polyphemus who created a salty well on the Acropolis of Athens with a blow of his trident.

Symbols sacred to this son of Shatarupa include the cuckoo. The first Hindu marriage was supposedly that of this god's sister Prasuti, who gave birth to 60 daughters. One of this deity's lesser-known consorts was Priti, the personification of affection and delight; his other consorts included his niece Rati. This god once evaded the guard Nandini to awake Shiva and felt the wrath of his third eye, resulting in his transformation into a heap of ash. Often associated with flowers and bees, name this Hindu god of love.

Nine slaves cut each other's throats in an effort to obtain this figure's whetstone. He was sometimes called Herion when he led the wild hunt, and his main objective during the hunt was to kill a skogsra. In one story, he visits a king named Geirrod while disguised as the island farmer Grimnir, only to be tortured between two fires. In another story he appears as the ferryman Harbard, who insults this god's son by Fjorgyn or Jord, and in the Volsung Saga he places a sword in the Barnstokk while disguised as a tall, one-eyed man. He learns all of the world's news each day from his ravens Huginn and Muninn. Name this father of Thor.

Pharyllus stole this object and gave it to Ariston. The sons of Phegeus were killed trying to take this object and a peplos to Delphi. It was dedicated to the temple of Athena Pronoea by Acarnan and Amphoterus, who obtained it after their mother's prayer turned them into adults so they could avenge their father Alcmaeon, who died trying to acquire this object. Eriphyle accepted this object as a bribe from Polyneices, who had inherited it as an heirloom of the Theban royal house. Identify this doom-laden piece of bling made by Hephaestus for Cadmus's wife.

The Shilluk people believed that their creator god Jo-Uk created a sacred white cow out of this entity. In Dinka mythology, Aiwei's mother was impregnated by this entity. Abtu and Anet were two creatures that resided in this entity and were tasked with warning Ra. According to the Famine Stele, Djoser requested help from Hapy and a god residing at Elephantine to control this body. The sarcophagus containing Osiris' body was placed in it, and its annual cycle coincided with his death and resurrection. Khnum was one of the primary gods of what major river of Egypt?

After Loki's insults to this deity fail to elicit a response at a banquet, Loki proceeds to denounce Frey's servant Beyla; Loki's insults to this goddess are preceded by her pouring a horn of mead for Loki. One son of this deity used a shield as a boat and lived in a hall located in a yew dale. Another child of this goddess was engaged to the dwarf Alviss, who turned to stone after being tricked by this goddess's husband. This mother of Thrud and Ullr was the victim of a prank that resulted in a commission for the sons of Ivaldi, who produced a gold headpiece for her after Loki cut off her hair. Name this wife of Thor.

In one myth, these creatures assume their present form when Ayas'e cuts up two cannibalistic old women into small pieces. In another myth, this creature once received a feather from each bird, only to lose them after becoming arrogant, explaining why it will only come out at night and lives in caves. One of these animals placed Hunahpu's head in a ball court after he was decapitated in their namesake House in Xibalba. The Mayan death god Camazotz had the head of what animal commonly associated with vampires?

Apollodorus credits these figures with killing Agrius and Thoas. They revealed the method by which Oeneus's wife avenged the deaths of Toxeus and Plexippus. In the Theogony, Hesiod calls them the siblings of Eirene, Dike, and Eunomia, and states that they are the children of Nyx or of Zeus and Themis. Althaea overheard these figures discussing the connection between a piece of wood and her son Meleager. Hesychius states that they appear seven days after the birth of an infant at the family hearth. Name these divine personifications of destiny named Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos.

A group of Etruscan haruspices were killed for ordering a statue of this figure to be moved to a dark place after lightning had struck the original in the Comitium. During a famine, the people of Rome gave this man food and as much land as he could plough in one day. When an enemy came over the Janiculum, this man fought alongside Titus Herminius and Spurius Lartius before telling them to retreat from the Pons Sublicius. Name this legendary Roman hero who swam across the Tiber in armor after single- handedly defending Rome from the Etruscans while the bridge he stood on was disassembled.

Rejection by an attractive man led this figure to create the first ohia tree, and she killed several other men during various sled races. This figure led an army to battle an owl ghost-god who protected a giant who could transform into a dragon. While migrating, she incubated her mother's egg till it hatched into her sister, who carries the clouds. Her other siblings include the king of the sharks, Ka-moo-alii. Name this resident of the crater Halemaumau, the Hawaiian goddess of fire, wind, lightning, and volcanoes.

The Kouretes impaired this figure's hearing, leading to his eventual downfall. He was the indirect creator of the men of the Bronze Age, since his actions resulted in the birth of the Meliae. In some myths, this god defeated Ophion, after which he ruled over an idyllic realm. He set Campe to guard Tartarus, but she was killed when one of his sons freed the prisoners. He could be considered a brother of Aphrodite, who was born when he castrated his father, while his other sisters included Metis and Rhea. Name this sickle-wielding son of Uranus who was deposed by his own son Zeus.

In the Puranas, this figure owns an all-knowing parrot, and attacks the city of Bhallata in order to defeat Sasidhvaja, who sadly has to forego the pleasure of being killed by this figure. His wife lives in Sinhale and bears Vijayajaya and Kirana, who is blessed by Durga with superhuman powers. This husband of Padma is taught by Parasurama, who later reveals that they are both incarnations of the same god. This figure is often depicted with a flaming sword in his right hand, riding his white horse Devadatta. The Kali Yuga ends with the appearance of what final avatar of Vishnu?

Nemesis refused to do this to Aura and arranged for her rape instead. This was the ultimate fate of Aglauros for barring her sister's doorway. The jilted Iphis called on Aphrodite, who did this to Anaxarete, and Hermes did this to the shepherd Battus, who saw the god stealing cattle. Zeus resolved an annoying paradox by doing this to Laelaps and the Teumessian Fox. After Apollo and Artemis killed her 14 children, this fate befell Niobe atop Mount Sipylus. One man avoided this fate by looking at his shield's reflection, and Ovid states that Atlas was killed in this manner by that man, the hero Perseus. Identify this fatal transformation that could be produced by looking at Medusa.

One of these figures feigned death when he reached the Temple of the Jealous Woman. Another member of this group discovered gold on his farm after he was robbed, but did not take any, which was part of his ten trials. In one story, this group travels across an ocean to the Conference of the Magical Peach by using each of their special powers. The leader of this group had 18 years' worth of dreams in the time it took his millet to cook. Transportation aids owned by this group include the foldable donkey of Elder Zhang Guo and the Iron Crutch of Li. Name this octet from Taoist mythology who obtained eternal life.

The Ardre VIII stone depicts this figure flying on eagle wings. Some sources state that he and his brothers lived with three Valkyries, while other sources state that he married the swan maiden Hervor. Bodvild's father Nidud captured this figure and crippled him; in revenge, he killed Nidud's sons and used their skulls and eyes to make goblets and jewels. In English lore, he is associated with a mound where travelers who leave a horse and some money overnight will supposedly find the horse reshod. Identify this smith from Germanic and Norse mythology.

One of this deity's temples featured a choir of blind singers accompanied by a blind harpist. A baton known as a hrp [herp] was used to touch offerings directed to this deity. Psalm 104 may have influenced a song to this deity that begins with the line "How manifold it is, what thou hast made", and which was found in the city of Ay. This deity's worship was abolished by Horemheb. Amarna was the cult center of this god, whose cult became prominent during the reign of the father of Tutankhamen. FTP, name this subject of a monotheistic belief system established by Amenhotep IV.

The width and lifespan of the branches of a tree sacred to this figure predicted the fates of Vespasian's children. The Regia, built by Numa, contained objects sacred to this figure; those objects' shakings predicted the death of Julius Caesar. After this husband of Neriene performed an action which caused Hersilia to weep, Iris brought Hersilia to a hill where she was deified as Hora. That action was the deification of Quirinus. This god also impregnated a woman who had been made a Vestal Virgin by her uncle Amulius. Rhea Silvia bore Romulus and Remus to what Roman god of war?

Pelias spared only Aeson after learning of a prophecy that he would be killed by a descendant of a figure with this name. That figure of this name was the father of Athamas, who tried to fulfill the terms of a false prophecy by killing his own son Phrixus. That brother of Dorus and Xuthus shares this name with a figure in the Aeneid who was offered Deiopea as a wife in return for releasing Eurus and Notus by hitting the side of a cave with a turned spear. That god's gift was mistaken for a container of wine by Odysseus's crew, who opened it and found themselves blown back to his island. Name this god who gave Odysseus a sack of winds.

This figure landed in a golden cup of wine seven years after being blown away from a crystal bower. Her first husband played a game of fidchell against her second husband to win a kiss from her that reawakens her memories. She was transformed into a pool of water, then an enormous, beautiful, purple fly by the jealous Fuamnach. Eochaid failed to identify this twice-born wife of his amongst 50 identical women at the sidh of Bri Leith after she left with her first husband, the god Midir. Identify this Celtic heroine of a namesake epic about her "Wooing."

One of this woman's sons conquered the land beyond the Thyamis with the Epeirots, and another killed Areius, king of Teuthrania. This mother of Cestrinus and Pergamus pointed out the Erineos to her husband near some fig trees. Menelaus threatened to kill her son Molossus if she did not die herself. While this woman was mourning at a Nereid statue, Hermione accused this woman of depriving her of sex. Calchas gave a prophecy which caused Odysseus to kill her son Astyanax by throwing him from a battlement after the death of her husband, who was. Name this wife of Hector.

A hill near Troy was called Batieia by humans, but the gods named it Myrina after one of these figures. According to Herodotus, these figures wandered about singing at midday in groups of one or two. One of these people came from Scythia to provoke a battle with the Athenians at the marriage of Phaedra and Theseus. Thersites was killed for gouging out the eyes of one of these people who killed Machaon, and whose corpse inspired love in Achilles. Penthesilea and Antiope were two of these people, who were visited by Heracles during his labor to obtain the girdle of their queen Hippolyta. Identify this tribe of warrior women.

Hector's bones were buried adjacent to a fountain named for this man. The king of Plataea, Damasistratus, buried some men murdered by this man, and a famine that began during his reign ended when Menoeceus committed suicide. Most sources state that this man died in exile and was buried by Theseus. As an infant, he was exposed on Mount Cithaeron with his legs bound, and he was healed and raised by Periboea. After his wife hung herself, this man used a pin from her dress to blind himself. Identify this man who solved the riddle of the Sphinx and unwittingly married his mother Jocasta.

This myth system's cosmology includes a world tree on which the sun goddess hangs her belt at the end of each day. Goddesses in this myth system include a goddess of destiny named Laima, a mother goddess of dead souls named Velu Mate, and the aforementioned sun goddess Saule. Sky gods in this myth system include the supreme deity Dievs, and a god of oaks and thunder who fights the devil; that thunder god is the counterpart of the Slavic Perun, and is named Perkunas. Name this myth system preserved in part in the dainas of Latvia and Lithuania.

In Egyptian mythology this entity was represented by a goddess named Bat, who was eventually combined with Hathor. In the Bhagavata Purana this entity is said to be part of a dolphin, and in Ovid's Metamorphoses it is said to house the homes of the gods. In East Asian myth, it is a river spanned by a flock of crows on the 7th day of the 7th month of each year that separates a couple the rest of the year. One story says that this entity formed when the infant Heracles was pushed away from suckling at Hera's breast. Name this heavenly feature that has an appearance resembling a stream of a dairy product.

This deity made a contract that all of the gods must die, including himself, so that the sun would move again, but hid himself when all the other gods died. In another story, this god cooked himself alive in a kettle, starting the trend of ritual self-torture among his people. This owner of the ehecailacacozcatl [eh-HEY-kay-lah-kah-KOZE-caht-el] is the patron of Ullamaliztli. This evil personification of Venus forced Xochiquetzal to eat forbidden fruit and ravished her. Often depicted as a monster with reversed feet, a skeleton, or a dog-headed man, name this god of lightning and bad luck, the twin brother of Quetzalcoatl.

A king who shared this god's name had a daughter named Theonoe and was married to the Nereid Psamathe. This god's sons Polygonus and Telegonus died after foolishly challenged Heracles to wrestling matches. In Virgil's Georgics, this god advises Aristaeus to sacrifice 12 animals and leave the corpses, one of which produces a swarm of bees three days later. He also advised a king on how to return to Sparta from Egypt, where that king captured this god while he was sleeping among his herd of seals. Name this shapeshifting son of Poseidon, Oceanus or Nereus, a god sometimes known as the "Old Man of the Sea."

In the Lokasenna, Tyr defends this god as being the noblest and bravest of the gods, saying that he would never harm a mortal. Adam of Bremen describes an erect giant wooden penis dedicated to this god in the Temple of Uppsala, and the Ynglinga Saga claims that this god fathered the kings of Sweden. At Ragnarok, this god defeats the jotunn Belli with the horn of a deer because he gave up his giant-killing sword to obtain his wife, but he retained possession of the folding ship Skidbladnir, and the glowing boar Gullinbursti. Name this Vanir god, the son of Njord.

This man's father accidentally killed Eurytion during the hunt for the Calydonian Boar, and killed Phocus with the help of this man's uncle Telamon. This man's shade was said to have married that of Medea in the Elysian Fields. After this man stabbed Tenes, his servant Mnemon was killed for failing to remind him of the consequences of killing Apollo's sons. This man was also responsible for wounding and then healing the Mysian king Telephus. He commanded the Greeks to sacrifice the Trojan maiden Polyxena on his grave, a task accomplished by his son, who also killed King Priam and took Andromache as a concubine. Name this father of Neoptolemus, a nearly- invulnerable son of Thetis who killed Hector.

This creature brought daylight to the Inuit. In Lenape mythology, a Rainbow one of these creatures received fire from the Creator to warm the animals of earth, but the smoke destroyed his beautiful voice. A three-legged one of these creature guided Jimmu-Tenno to Yamato-no-kuni, and was named Yatagarasu. A vain one loses some cheese to a fox in a fable told by Aesop, and in Greek myth one of these animals was punished for tattling on Coronis. Badb took the form of this animal, one of which perched on Cuchulainn to prove his death. Identify this bird whose feathers were turned black by Apollo.

One god of this phenomenon will not enter the houses of people who are having sex, and rides a chariot driven by A Xiang. That god, who obtained mastery of this phenomenon after eating a peach from heaven and growing bird wings, is named Lei Gong, and he is accompanied by a goddess who helps create this phenomenon with flashing mirrors that also create light. Another god of this phenomenon is known for eating belly buttons, and is often seen with the wind god Fujin. Identify this phenomenon created in Shinto myth by the drum-banging god Raijin, who accompanies the storm god Susano'o, and in Norse myth by Thor.

This figure left a golden honeycomb at a shrine on Mount Eryx for Aphrodite. Acastus lost a hunting competition when a magic sword created by this figure allowed Peleus to kill a large heap of animals. This man killed a former employer by pouring boiling water on him as he bathed, after this man inadvertently revealed himself by helping out Cocalus by tying an ant to a string to thread it through a shell. After killing his nephew, who was named Talos or Perdix, this man fled from Athens to a place where he built a wooden cow suit on wheels for Pasiphae. He also gave a ball of yarn to Ariadne which she passed on to Theseus. Identify this architect of the Labyrinth who built wings for himself and his son Icarus.

In the Grimnismal, Odin tells Agnar that Thor sits as judge at this place, which he reaches by wading through the rivers Kormt and Ormt; Odin also states that its inhabitants include Duneyr, Durathror, Dvalinn and Dainn. It lies near the source of all cold rivers—a spring named Hvergelmir—as well as a font of wisdom named Mimisbrunnr, and the home of the Norns. It also shelters the hawk Vedrfolnir, who sends insulting messages via the squirrel Ratatosk down to the dragon Nidhogg, who dwells near its base. Odin hung himself for nine days and nights on what ash tree of Norse myth?

A group of creatures including Mesetet, Petet, and Tjetet plotted with Tefen to do this to a noblewoman's son after she refused entry to Isis. Isis made a creature out of Ra's saliva that did this to him, after which he gave up his secret name. In Hindu myth, the demoness Putana tried to do this to the infant Krishna by breastfeeding him, and Shiva survived but had his throat turned blue when he swallowed a substance that would normally have had this effect. Name this possibly-fatal result of a scorpion sting or snake bite.

A bird once laid seven eggs on this deity's knee, including an iron egg that hatched into a storm cloud. This goddess wandered for seven centuries, became pregnant by the sea or wind, and wandered for another seven centuries until she gave birth. This goddess's son won a music contest but lost his prize, the maiden Aino, because she preferred drowning to marrying him. Known as the "Daughter of Air", identify this Finnish creation goddess and mother of Väinämäinen who was also known as Luonnotar.

This figure's four fingers and toes were said to touch the four points that represented the directions north, south, east and west. One of this goddess's sons used a maqet, or celestial ladder, to hide from his brother; as a result she was often depicted often depicted on the lids of sarcophagi. Her father prevented her from copulating with her husband after Thoth stole moonlight for her, but the moonlight allowed her to give birth to five children, including Nephthys and Isis. Name this sky goddess who was married to Geb.

As he lay dying, this figure told his killer about the uncreated island of Oskapt, where the gods and Surt will mingle their "sword-liquor." This figure owned the sword Ridill, which was used later to cut his heart out. His slayer had to dig many trenches for his blood to run into and gained the ability to understand birds after tasting this figure's blood. This son of Hreidmar counted among his possessions the Tarnhelm, or helm of terror, as well as the cursed hoard of Andvari. He was dealt a mortal blow by the sword Gram as he slithered over a pit containing a hero coached by his brother Regin. Name this dwarf whose greed turned him into a dragon, who was slain by Sigurd.

Hesiod's Theogony describes this figure's palace as being propped up by silver columns, and says that she was the first to ally with Zeus during the Titanomachy; in gratitude, Zeus shelters her children by Pallas, namely Bia, Zelus, Cratos, and Nike. Hesiod also calls her the oldest and greatest of the Oceanids, and says that Iris occasionally brings a golden flagon to this figure's home as part of a ceremony whose participants lie breathless for one year and are banned from the councils of the gods for nine years if they forswear themselves. This figure's namesake feature gives rise to Titaressus and Cocytus, and was the site of Thetis's attempt to make Achilles invulnerable. The boatman Charon ferries souls across what main river of Hades?

These figures possessed the knife used to kill Itys, and earlier attended his parents' wedding as torchbearers. In the Orphic Hymns they are the children of Hades and Persephone, but the Theogony states that their siblings are the giants and the Meliae. Telemachus refused to force Penelope to remarry for fear that she would invoke these figures to curse him, an act performed by Oedipus on his sons. They were given patronship of Athens after losing a case in the Areopagus against Orestes, who was pursued by them after murdering his mother. Tisiphone, Megaira and Alekto were what trio of winged, whip-wielding goddesses who punished mortals for crimes?

Two of this god's sons traveled in different directions to spread knowledge of the names of all plants to humanity. Another of his children sons gave a couple a divine golden wedge that signaled the site for construction of the capital of the empire in which he was worshipped. In his native language, this god's name literally translates to "Sea Foam." This god pardoned two Cañaris who attempted to molest two women in the aftermath of a deluge sent by this god. This sender of the Unu Pachakuti was the husband of Mama Quilla. Name this father of Inti, the supreme creator and storm god of the Inca pantheon.

This god was often portrayed as a lion or a lion-headed colossus, and was often shown holding a lion-headed mace. His father raped his mother four times, the second time disguised as a gatekeeper; he was born from that union. He was known as "lord of the great dwelling" and "the burner." As Meshlamtea, he was corrupted while he tried to conquer the land he would later rule; that land was Arallu, where he also served as judge. He was also said to be the husband of a goddess who was sometimes said to be married to Gugalana. Name this Babylonian lord of the underworld and husband of Ereshkigal.

In one myth, this god is struck with a branding iron and then flayed, explaining how the leopard got his spots. This god's cult centers included Ombos, Sepermeru and Avaris. This god entered a competition to race stone boats, but lost because his opponent cheated with a painted wooden boat. During one battle, this god lost a testicle but took out his foe's eye. He swallowed some semen while eating his beloved lettuce, and was therefore considered subservient. The Shabaka Stone says Geb gave this deity the upper plateau of his lands; later, Geb revoked the judgement and gave all of Egypt to this god's foe, who was his nephew. Name this Egyptian god of the desert who killed his brother Osiris and fought Horus.

One of these places sometimes called "Salamanca" is home to a god who is invoked in the "flame virgin" dance. In another of these places, a flock of quails pecking at certain objects resulted in the varying heights of humans. Supay is one god associated with these places, one of which is called Uku Pacha. Another one ruled by Hun Came was home to a river of blood; the crazy god Ixtab guided people to that example of this type of realm. In order to recreate humanity, Quetzalcoatl collected bones from one of these places. Name these places exemplified by Xibalba and Mictlan.

This man's only daughter died in the act of donating blood in an attempt to heal a leprous woman. One son of this man fathered Morien with a black princess, while another was tasked with retrieving a white brachet at King Arthur's wedding. According to some sources, a more famous son of this man fell in love with Blanchfleur and healed the Fisher King. This man started a blood feud by killing King Lot, but spent much of his life chasing a creature that made noises like a pack of yelping hounds. Name this father of Lamorak and Percival, a king who hunted the Questing Beast.

These figures came to the kingdom of Gelanor soon after Poseidon had punished Inachus for claiming that the land belonged to Hera, and they introduced a rite of Demeter named Thesmophoria to Greece. One member of this group had a son named Abas, whose children Acrisius and Proetus struggled for power in the womb. That woman was married to Lynceus. After a banquet, the father of this group gave an order which only one, Hypermnestra, disobeyed. In the underworld, they eternally attempt to bring water from a stream with perforated jugs. Identify these women, forty-nine of whom killed their husbands on their wedding night.

Hadingus received aid from this figure and an old man, and realized that this figure can travel on water when he looked through the holes of the old man's cloak. This figure once crossed the river Gjoll and jumped over the gate of Hel while in the company of a bold god. On another occasion he won a race against Gullfaxi. He was conceived during a construction project whose payoff was Freya, the Sun, and the Moon, but construction stalled when his father Svadilfari was distracted by Loki, who had taken the form of a mare. Name this eight-legged horse, the mount of Odin.

One son of this god challenged a water goddess to a weaving contest after she attempted to vanquish humanity with a great flood. This god gave a subordinate a hen, a sand-filled snail, a palm nut, and a cat, or a golden chain, a bag of dirt, and a five-toed chicken, with which the subordinate created the world. This god's messengers included a chameleon named Agemo and a god with a half-black, half-red hat named Elegua. The father of Orunmila and superior of Obatala is, what chief Orisha who presides over the Yoruba pantheon?

This figure once kidnapped Tara, the wife of Brihaspati, sparking a war in which he allied with the asuras against the gods. He is often depicted as a bull, bird, or embryo, but only rarely as an adult. This son of Atri is married to the Nakshatras, and he was punished for favoring Rohini, but his other wives intervened and made his death periodic and temporary. Surya provides nourishing ocean water when this god is exhausted by the many gods feeding on his ambrosia. For 10 point, identify this god of poetry and the moon, whose namesake substance is consumed by the gods.

One attendant of this deity was the patron of manual labor; that attendant, or another figure with the same name, had four sons that were turned into oxen and used to plow Zealand away from the continent. This deity's messenger rode Hofvarpnir, and her attendants included Eir, the goddess of healing. Gna served this owner of the hall Fensalir, who was prompted by her son's nightmares about his own death to extract an oath from everything in the world, except for mistletoe, never to harm her son. Name this Norse goddess, the mother of Baldr and the wife of Odin.

The Homeric hymn to this figure mentions his birth "in the Dotian plain," and one myth asserts that he was born in his future cult center of Epidauros, where no one was allowed to die or give birth near the temple. Another of this figure's major temples had a spa watered by the spring of King Halkon and was located at Kos. Like Erichthonius, Athena gave this figure two vials of blood drawn from the left and right veins of Medusa, one of which was lethal poison. He was born after being rescued from the funeral pyre of his pregnant mother Coronis, and one myth about his death suggests that he was killed for accepting a bribe to bring Hippolytus back to life. Name this student of Chiron and son of Apollo, a great healer in Greek mythology.
